title: Where Does the Rain Go?
style: calm luminous paper-cut watercolour science storybook

pages.text: Rain lands on soil, grass, roofs and roads. Each landing is the start of a different journey.

quickWords.th: เส้นทางน้ำ

pages.text: Soil is like a sponge. It drinks the rain.
A sponge can fill up. Soil that is full of water is called saturated soil. When rain comes faster than full soil can take it in, water stays on top.

quickWords.th: ดินอิ่มน้ำ
อยู่ด้านบน

pages.text: Extra water flows across the ground. This flowing water is called runoff. It slides to lower places.

quickWords.th: น้ำไหลบ่าบนผิวดิน
พื้นที่ต่ำกว่า

pages.text: In towns, water slips into drains under the street.

quickWords.th: ท่อระบายน้ำ

pages.text: Drains lead to canals. Canals lead to rivers. Rivers carry water to the sea.
Some water waits in puddles and leaves. The sun lifts it back up as vapour. This is evaporation.
People also catch rain. Tanks, ponds and reservoirs keep it for dry days.

quickWords.th: ถังเก็บน้ำ
อ่างเก็บน้ำ

pages.text: Every drop of rain takes one of these journeys. Water that is stored can journey again another day.

quickWords.th: เส้นทางน้ำ
กักเก็บไว้

pages.text: Our paper boats follow the water downhill. Next time it rains, watch where the water goes!

quickWords.th: เรือกระดาษ
